h1: The 8 Best 49-Inch Ultrawide Monitors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best 49-inch ultrawide monitors of 2026, covering QD-OLED, VA and IPS Black options for gaming and work desks.
summary: The MSI MPG 491CQP is the best 49 inch ultrawide here, bringing QD-OLED contrast at the lowest entry price in the group. Samsung's G93SC is the faster, longer-warranted step up, and the G91SD adds HDMI 2.1 for consoles. For desks with several computers, look to the Dell U4924DW or Samsung S95UA with built-in KVM.
intro: Forget the diagonal. The spec that defines a 49 inch ultrawide is 5120 by 1440, which is two 2560 by 1440 panels stitched together with no bezel in the middle. You gain enormous horizontal workspace but only 1440 pixels of height, so the picture feels wide rather than razor sharp. Desk depth deserves a measuring tape before you click buy.

We ranked eight 49 inch ultrawides from their stated specs, weighing panel type, refresh rate, brightness, connectivity and warranty coverage. All sit in the $500 and up tier, so the order separates OLED from VA from IPS and games from office duty. Burn-in risk and warranty length get extra attention on the OLED models.

products.name: MSI MPG 491CQP QD-OLED
products.verdict: QD-OLED contrast at the lowest entry price here.
products.description:
The MSI MPG 491CQP is a 49 inch QD-OLED panel at 5120 by 1440, running at 144Hz with 0.03ms response and FreeSync Premium Pro. USB-C is built in, and the stand adjusts for tilt and height. Coverage runs 2 years.

It earns first place by pricing OLED contrast lower than any rival here. Samsung's G93SC refreshes at 240Hz and carries a longer warranty, but costs more, and for mixed gaming and work the speed gap rarely decides the purchase. The shorter warranty is the notable compromise, since OLED panels age with static content.

Buy it if you split time between games, spreadsheets and video, and want deep blacks without paying the top price. Skip it if the longest possible protection plan is your priority, or if you need a refresh rate beyond 144Hz.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G93SC
products.description:
Samsung's Odyssey G93SC is a curved 1800R QD-OLED at 5120 by 1440, with 240Hz refresh and 0.03ms response. Samsung quotes a million to one contrast and 99% DCI-P3 coverage. G-Sync, FreeSync Premium Pro and picture-by-picture are all supported, and a 3 year warranty backs it.

It trails the MSI only because of cost. Everything the MSI does, this one does faster, with an extra year of coverage, but the price gap sits in a tier where every model is already expensive. Compared with the G91SD below, the refresh rate is the main reason to pay more.

Buy it for fast competitive games or color-critical work. The caveat is the curve, which asks for a deep desk and some patience while you position it.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G91SD
products.verdict: QD-OLED with HDMI 2.1 and a metal build.
products.description:
The Odyssey G9 G91SD is a 49 inch QD-OLED at 5120 by 1440, with 144Hz, 0.03ms GtG and a million to one contrast figure. It supports FreeSync Premium Pro and G-Sync compatibility, includes HDMI 2.1 and USB-C, and wears a metal design with a 3 year warranty.

Third place comes from a refresh rate that trails the G93SC. What it gains is HDMI 2.1, which lets a modern console run at higher frame rates on a screen this wide. That makes it a more practical choice than the faster model if a console shares the desk.

Buy it for a mixed console and PC setup where the extra ports and the metal build count. Skip it if you want 240Hz, since the G93SC delivers it with the same QD-OLED panel type.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G91F
products.verdict: A curved VA with DisplayHDR 600 and auto source switching.
products.description:
Samsung's G91F is a curved 1000R VA panel at 5120 by 1440, with 144Hz refresh and 1ms GtG response. It peaks near 280 nits for DisplayHDR 600, adds FreeSync Premium Pro, picture-by-picture and automatic source switching, and carries a 3 year warranty.

It ranks fourth because VA cannot match OLED black levels or pixel speed. Its answer to the OLED models above is peace of mind: there is no burn-in concern, and the tight 1000R curve wraps closely around your view. Brightness is modest next to the G95C below.

Buy it if you prefer the look of VA and want reliable HDR for general use. Skip it if inky blacks matter most, since the cheaper MSI delivers that. Mind the desk depth too, because a 1000R curve is aggressive.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G95C
products.verdict: 1000 nit peak brightness, the highest here.
products.description:
The Odyssey G9 G95C is a curved 1000R VA at 5120 by 1440 with 240Hz refresh and 1ms GtG. Its 1000 nit peak is the brightest in this ranking. FreeSync Premium Pro and picture-by-picture are supported, though the warranty is not listed.

It sits fifth because brightness alone does not fix VA contrast. The OLED models above show deeper blacks, and the G91F undercuts it with similar traits at a slower 144Hz. What the G95C offers is highlight punch for HDR content and a sunlit room.

Buy it for rooms with heavy daylight where HDR highlights matter more than shadows. Skip it if you want OLED blacks, and confirm the warranty terms with the seller, since our data does not state them.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G95SD
products.verdict: The only pick with a glare free coating.
products.description:
Samsung's G95SD is a 49 inch QD-OLED with a Glare-Free coating, the only one in this guide that has it. It runs 5120 by 1440 at 240Hz with 0.03ms GtG, adds built-in Wi-Fi and SmartThings, and Gaming Hub for streaming games without a PC. Three years of warranty cover it.

It ranks sixth because buyer feedback is the weakest in the group, and the coating mutes contrast slightly compared with the standard glossy QD-OLED models. Still, it offers a strong answer to reflections that no other pick provides.

Buy it if windows or lamps spoil your view and you want OLED speed. Skip it if feedback weight matters to you, or if you want the sharpest contrast, which the G93SC delivers with the same refresh rate.

products.name: Dell UltraSharp U4924DW
products.verdict: A productivity monitor with an automatic KVM.
products.description:
The Dell UltraSharp U4924DW is a 49 inch IPS Black at 5120 by 1440, covering 100% sRGB. It refreshes at 60Hz, the lowest here by design, and loads in an automatic KVM, USB-C with 90W power delivery, 2.5GbE Ethernet and 11 USB ports, plus dual 9W speakers.

It ranks seventh because 60Hz limits it for gaming, while the Samsung Business S95UA below it undercuts it on price and runs at 120Hz. Where it wins is as a docking hub: one cable can power a laptop and link peripherals, networks and a second computer.

Buy it for multi-computer office desks and laptop docking. Skip it if you play games, as every Odyssey above is far smoother.

products.name: Samsung Business S95UA
products.verdict: A built in KVM at a lower price than the Dell.
products.description:
Samsung's Business S95UA is a 49 inch curved 1000R VA at 5120 by 1440 and 120Hz. It packs a built-in KVM, USB-C with 90W power delivery, Ethernet, speakers and DisplayHDR 400, with a 3 year business warranty.

It finishes last because HDR and panel quality are modest. The Dell U4924DW looks better for color, though it refreshes at only 60Hz, so the Samsung wins on motion and on cost. That makes it a fair compromise for work-first desks.

Buy it for an office setup where one screen must serve two computers and charge a laptop on a tighter budget. Skip it if OLED matters or if you want gaming extras, since the Odyssey line serves those goals better.

whatMatters.detail: Panel type shapes contrast, brightness and color. QD-OLED delivers deep blacks, VA tends to reach high brightness, and IPS Black favors color accuracy. OLED can show burn-in with static content, so the warranty carries weight. Read the panel name in the product title, then check how long coverage runs.

Resolution on these monitors is 5120 by 1440, equal to two 2560 by 1440 screens side by side. It gives huge width but not 4K height, so text is sharp rather than razor crisp. Confirm the pixel count in the title or spec table before buying, especially if you are expecting a taller image.

Refresh rate, in Hz, sets how smooth motion looks. Games feel better at 144Hz or 240Hz, while 60Hz is fine for documents. The Samsung G93SC and G95C list 240Hz, and the Dell lists 60Hz. Check the Hz figure in the listing, and note whether it applies over HDMI or only DisplayPort.

A KVM switch lets two computers share one keyboard and mouse, and USB-C with 90W power delivery can charge a laptop through a single cable. The Dell U4924DW and Samsung S95UA include both. Look for KVM, USB-C and the wattage in the spec table, then count the downstream ports.

Curve is measured as a radius. A tighter number such as 1000R wraps more around you, and a looser one such as 1800R feels flatter. A tighter curve also needs more desk depth, roughly 28 inches. Find the R value in the specs, and measure your desk before ordering.

cards.label: QD-OLED
cards.text: Deep blacks and fast response. MSI 491CQP, G93SC, G91SD and G95SD use it.

cards.label: VA
cards.text: Brighter peaks and no burn in worry. G91F, G95C and S95UA use it.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to QD-OLED unless the room is very bright.

cards.text: You want OLED for less. The MSI MPG 491CQP is the entry point.

faq.a: Likely, but measure first. A 49 inch panel is around 45 inches wide, and curved models like the Samsung G91F at 1000R need generous depth. Check both width and the stand footprint before ordering.
Expecting 4K sharpness. At 5120 by 1440, the MSI MPG 491CQP is very wide but not tall, so pixel density feels closer to a 27 inch 1440p screen than a 4K one.

faq.q: Is QD-OLED worth it over VA?
faq.a: For contrast and speed, yes. The MSI MPG 491CQP is the cheapest QD-OLED here, while VA options such as the Samsung G91F offer brightness and no burn-in worry. Pick OLED unless your room is very bright.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use DisplayPort for the full refresh rate on a PC. The Samsung G91SD adds HDMI 2.1 for consoles. Then set the resolution to 5120 by 1440 and enable FreeSync or G-Sync in the monitor menu.

faq.q: How do I limit burn in?
faq.a: Vary static content, use screen savers and keep brightness reasonable on QD-OLED models like the Samsung G93SC. Check the warranty too: MSI offers 2 years, while the Samsung OLED models list 3 years.
Yes. The Dell U4924DW and Samsung Business S95UA both include a KVM switch, so two computers can share one keyboard and mouse. Both also provide USB-C with 90W charging for a laptop.

finalTake: Most buyers should start with the MSI MPG 491CQP for OLED contrast without the highest price. Step up to the Samsung G93SC when 240Hz and three years of coverage justify the premium. Office users with more than one computer are better served by the Dell U4924DW or Samsung S95UA, and bright rooms may prefer a VA Odyssey.
